column1: # Logging functions. One row per function, per task it belongs to. Tab-separated; see finder.py for the rules.

column7: summary
Logs a message at the info level, or returns a record to add fields to.
Logs a message at the warn level, or returns a record to add fields to.
Logs a message at the error level, or returns a record to add fields to.
Logs a message at the debug level, or returns a record to add fields to.
Logs a message at trace, the finest level, or returns a record to add fields to.
Logs a message at the most severe level, or returns a record; it does not end the program.
Logs a message at a level you pass, or returns a record to add fields to.
Holds a sink that writes to stderr or stdout, in colour only on a terminal.
Holds a sink that appends records to a UTF-8 file, rotating it by size or by day.
Holds a sink that queues records for a worker thread to write to another sink.
Attaches a sink to the logger, which keeps a pointer to it and does not own it.
Detaches one sink; removing one that was never added does nothing.
Detaches every sink, without destroying any of them.
Returns how many sinks are attached to the logger.
Adds a named text field to the record and returns the record for the next call.
Adds a named integer field, which stays a number in JSON output.
Adds a named unsigned 64-bit integer field.
Adds a named floating-point field.
Adds a named true or false field.
Adds a named pointer field, such as the address of an object.
Adds a named field holding a point in time.
Adds a named field holding a length of time, such as how long a step took.
Adds a filesystem error as fields: its message, its code and any system error code.
Adds a named field from a value you built yourself, of any supported kind.
Holds one field value: null, boolean, number, text, pointer, time or time span.
Sets the message and sends the record; a record that is never sent logs nothing.
Sends the record without a message, for a record that is only fields.
Records the file, line and procedure the record came from.
Sends a finished record straight to every attached sink.
Sets or returns the lowest level the logger emits; LOG_OFF silences it.
Returns true if a record at a level would be emitted, to skip building costly messages.
Returns a level's name, such as "WARN", or its number if it has no name.
Returns a level's three-letter name, such as "WRN".
Reads a level from a name or number in any case; returns false if it is unknown.
Returns the syslog severity number for a level.
Returns a child logger that adds one field to every record it makes.
Returns a child logger with its own component name and the parent's sinks.
Sets or returns the logger's component name, attached to every record it makes.
Returns the one process-wide logger; LogInit gives it a sink and LogShutdown closes it.
Flushes every sink attached to the logger.
Flushes one sink on its own.
Closes a sink and releases what it holds; every kind of sink closes the same way.
Holds the plain-text formatter; its fields set the timestamp, colour and call site.
Appends a record as one line of text to a buffer, without clearing it first.
Holds a formatter that writes each record as one line of JSON.
Holds the interface every sink implements: Write, Flush, Close and DroppedCount.
Writes one record to a sink; the method a sink of your own overrides.
Returns how many records a sink could not write; the count never resets.
Sets the one handler told when a sink fails, or 0 to stop the reports.
